Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models

paper.arxiv.2211.03540

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2211.03540v2. Timed human-model QuALITY evaluation and controlled-selection limitations establish oversight protocol scope; it does not establish solved scalable oversight or production reliability. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The authors say the controlled multiple-choice setting, answer revelation and removal of high-performing participants limit applicability, and the observed confident errors do not validate the protocol for high-stakes oversight of more capable future systems.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The experiment compared unaided humans, a 52B helpful RLHF dialog model and human–model teams on MMLU and 5-minute-limit QuALITY questions; human conditions used 100 sampled validation questions per experiment.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Surge AI recruited/trained/paid two groups of five participants; one unusually strong unaided participant per task was excluded, leaving four per task in reported results. Participants received answer feedback and at least$20 per active-work hour.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Reported individual accuracy increased from 57.2% unaided to 75.4% with model help on MMLU and from 48.6% to 76.8% on timed QuALITY; assisted confidence-weighted group accuracy was 78.0% and 86.0% respectively.
